name: The Grace Period
label: Audio Dregs
lede: Chris Ott was a Boston drummer and a Pitchfork critic, and the Grace Period was the loop music he made on the side, from an Audio Dregs cassette in the '90s to zip files on a blog.

eras.title: One drummer, a tape deck and the Mast brothers
eras.text: Chris Ott was a Boston drummer who, in his label's words, started making electronic music on his own out of nervous habit; his own archive dates the work to 1995. His outlet was Audio Dregs, the tiny label brothers Eric and Evan Mast started around 1996, which put out a Grace Period cassette and then, in 1998, a CD.

years.cap: The Grace Period's Audio Dregs cassette, ADR 17, in Jon Hills' stack of '90s demo tapes, c. 1997 · Photo: Jonathan Hills
q: began making electronic music on his own years ago just out of nervous habit
years.src: Audio Dregs: Dynasty (Bandcamp)
years.h: Before any CD, a Grace Period tape marked "ad 17"
years.p: The label on the cassette in Jon Hills' stack fits Audio Dregs' ADR numbering, which reached ADR 025 by 1998. Audio Dregs later described this stage as years of micro-run cassettes, CD-Rs and 7"s.
years.xp:
Audio Dregs' bio pitched the project as a boy-girl group from NYC and Boston, or maybe just Ott, one drummer from Boston. It added that what the Grace Period is "changes with the seasons."

The label also insisted the sound came before the machines: it is computer music now, the bio said, but it sounded much the same before any computers were used.

years.src: Discogs: The Capital Suite, Bekampa Tramset · Valley Advocate: Mark Alan Miller
years.h: Ott co-produces [[The Capital Suite|9bfdd332-bfe5-4333-bb59-0882b5253b5c]] at the Slaughterhouse in Amherst
years.p: The Skidmore College band, with Jon Hills on vocals and guitar, cuts Bekampa Tramset with engineer Mark Alan Miller. The credits read "Produced by Mark Alan Miller, with Chris Ott (aka The Grace Period) and The Capital Suite."
years.xp:
The Slaughterhouse, a studio Miller later owned, was in the Valley Advocate's words a small, stark building on its own down an Amherst dirt road. Jim Hemingway and the band's Jamie Kennard mastered the record in February 1998.

It came out on Old Colony Recordings, a label with a PO box in Duxbury, Massachusetts, as catalog number COL001.

years.src: Discogs: The Grace Period, Bekampa Tramset · The Grace Period: Collected Works 1995-2012 · Discogs: The Capital Suite, Bekampa Tramset
years.h: Two different CDs called Bekampa Tramset come out in 1998
years.p: The Grace Period's is Audio Dregs ADR 025, 20 tracks on Discogs. The Capital Suite's, which Ott co-produced, is nine songs on Old Colony.
years.xp:
Discogs lists 20 tracks, opening with The Ring Wraiths and closing with March of the Wring Wraiths, with Room 237, Welcome To Bali and The Miles Standish Monument in between. Ott's own archive of the album has 15.

The monument stands in Duxbury, the same town as Old Colony's PO box. Neither record explains the shared title.

eras.title: From green vinyl to Dynasty
eras.text: Audio Dregs gave the Grace Period a 7" and then a proper album, Dynasty, recorded in Boston between 1998 and 2001. Ott was writing for Pitchfork at the same time, and the reviews that came in could not agree on how many people were in the band.

years.cap: The Et In Arcadia Ego 7" on Audio Dregs, 1999
years.src: Discogs: Et In Arcadia Ego · Discogs: Sound Of Garden 2 · EvilSponge: Dynasty · SoundCloud: The Grace Period
years.h: Audio Dregs presses 300 green copies of Et In Arcadia Ego
years.p: ADR 032, a limited 7". The B-sides are Do You Believe In Vitamins? and Fuck Amen.
years.xp:
When Fuck Amen turned up on the Japanese compilation Sound Of Garden 2 (Philter, December 2002), it was listed as Fsck Amen.

The title track resurfaced on Dynasty. EvilSponge's review said it "captures the sheer intimidating majesty of life in a dramatic way", and it is still the most played track on the band's SoundCloud.

years.src: Discogs: The Sensualists, Adaptations
years.h: A Grace Period remix for label-mates the Sensualists
years.p: Spacial Bodies (The Grace Period Remix) is track four on the Sensualists' Adaptations, Audio Dregs ADR 036.

years.src: Discogs: For Friends
years.h: Best Of Boston turns up first on a Tomlab compilation
years.p: The track lands on For Friends, a joint release by Germany's Tomlab and Audio Dregs (tom 15 / ADR 040), ahead of the album.

years.src: Discogs: 1 Mile North, Glass Wars · Mutual Skies: 1 Mile North, The Sunken Nest · Discogs: Old Colony Recordings
years.h: Old Colony's second CD is [[1 Mile North|b0d6108a-3dd5-479d-b518-803f54b3ba45]]'s Glass Wars
years.p: Old Colony, the Duxbury label behind the Capital Suite record, puts out Jon Hills' new project as COL002. Ott later wrote that it traded online, at shows in Brooklyn and out of his Boston apartment.
years.xp: Mutual Skies, the Cape Cod label Discogs says Old Colony now trades as, later wrote of 1 Mile North, "whose debut album Glass Wars we released over twenty years ago (as Old Colony Recordings)."

years.src: Discogs: Dynasty · AllMusic: Dynasty · EvilSponge: Dynasty · Audio Dregs: Dynasty (Bandcamp)
yt: I Can See My Breath, from Dynasty
years.h: Dynasty is built from loops recorded in Boston, 1998 to 2001
years.p: Audio Dregs ADR 041, (P) 2001: twelve tracks in 43 minutes, including Best Of Boston, Et in Arcadia Ego and Bartley Ride Armor.
years.xp:
AllMusic heard sampled strings, a loose-limbed trip-hop beat and a lonesome falsetto fragment on My Girlfriend. EvilSponge counted two loops playing against each other with samples on top: "It's not a lot of 'content', but it creates a rich, full sound."

Audio Dregs' copy billed it as the Grace Period's "big CD debut," though Bekampa Tramset had come out on CD on the same label three years earlier.

years.src: AllMusic: Dynasty · Rawkblog: Top 5 Bands of Pitchfork Writers
years.h: Dynasty reaches shops and AllMusic signs off on it
years.p: Mark Richardson's AllMusic verdict, after a warning that leaning on loops "occasionally" grows tiresome. Rawkblog later reported that Pitchfork, where Ott wrote, gave it a 7.4.
years.xp:
Richardson called it a "solid collection of low-key electronic songs" and singled out the phase-shifted drums of Best Of Boston.

Per Rawkblog, the Pitchfork review called Ott's drumming "the heart and soul of this record." The original review could not be checked for this page.

years.cap: Static Caravan's insert from the Mod Killer 7", UK, 2002
years.src: Discogs: Mod Killer
years.h: Static Caravan in the UK presses Mod Killer on heavy vinyl
years.p: VAN 42, Mod Killer backed with Sunny And Share, heavyweight vinyl with two inserts. One insert advertises the label's Modyfied Toy Orchestra and Grace Period 7"s.

years.src: Penny Black Music: Dynasty · EvilSponge: Dynasty · Audio Dregs: Dynasty (Bandcamp)
years.h: Penny Black hears Portishead, as played by Americans
years.p: Cila Warncke calls Dynasty "a pastiche of Portishead and Lemonjelly" and "competent Sunday-morning music". She likes Paris Au Printemps, less so the vocals.
years.xp: Warncke described the band as a "Boston-based trio" and Dynasty as its second LP. EvilSponge counted two people. Audio Dregs' own bio allowed that it might be just Ott.

eras.title: The critic leaves Pitchfork and keeps remixing
eras.text: Ott's writing got louder than his records in these years: an exit from Pitchfork, and from 2006 the Shallow Rewards name. The Grace Period kept going in remixes and compilation tracks, and then went self-released.

years.src: Impose: Chris Ott interview · 333sound: The 33 1/3 author Q&A, Chris Ott
years.h: Ott leaves Pitchfork
years.p: He had been an editor and contributor there, and wrote the 33 1/3 book on Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures; afterwards he wrote for the Village Voice and Impose.

years.src: Discogs: Fat Jon & Styrofoam, The Same Channel · Discogs: We Are All Cotton-Hearted
years.h: Morr Music puts a Grace Period mix on a Styrofoam record
years.p: Upgrade (Grace Period Mix) is track D2 of Fat Jon & Styrofoam's The Same Channel (Morr MM071). In Malaysia, Best Of Boston turns up on Mü-Nest's We Are All Cotton-Hearted.

years.src: The Grace Period: Collected Works 1995-2012 · Shallow Rewards: About
years.h: Scry Site starts the self-released years
years.p: A two-track EP, Scry Site and Identify #9, posted for download. The same year Ott starts using the name Shallow Rewards online.

eras.title: Zip files on a Blogspot page
eras.text: With no label in the picture, the Grace Period became short EPs posted for free download. In December 2010 Ott gathered everything on one blog, Collected Works, and kept adding to it until 2012.

years.src: The Grace Period: Collected Works 1995-2012
years.h: Two new tracks, bmub and gooluhhh
years.p: The STRTCHS EP goes up as a download, the first Grace Period release since Scry Site.

years.src: Rawkblog: Top 5 Bands of Pitchfork Writers
years.h: Rawkblog lists the Grace Period among Pitchfork writers' bands
years.p: David Greenwald's top five calls Ott the drummer for "the neo-shoegazers Grace Period".
years.xp: Greenwald's opener on Ott: "one of the best writers in rock criticism when he's not busy being its bitterest." The same post is the source for Dynasty's 7.4 at Pitchfork.

years.src: The Grace Period: Collected Works 1995-2012 · Wikipedia: There Is Love in You
years.h: Four Tet's Angel Echoes gets an '82 remix
years.p: TLIU82 pairs There is Love in You '82, a remix of the opener of Four Tet's January 2010 album, with a track called Vision.

years.src: The Grace Period: Collected Works 1995-2012
years.h: Ott posts fifteen years of the Grace Period on one blog
years.p: Collected Works 1995-2010 puts the releases up as zip files, from Bekampa Tramset on. The title later stretched to 2012.

years.src: SoundCloud: The Grace Period · The Grace Period: Collected Works 1995-2012 · Apple Music: Mod Killer (single)
years.h: The SoundCloud goes up under the name Bartley Ride
years.p: Ott's SoundCloud uses the name of a Dynasty track, and gets seven uploads in one day, from Scry Site to Ghost in the Graveyard.
years.xp:
The profile line: "Celebrating the days of advertised oversampling ratios."

The same year brought Be S†ill My Bea†ing Hear†, a new title track plus three pieces dated 1998, and a digital Mod Killer single with Sunny and Share marked 2011.

years.src: The Grace Period: Collected Works 1995-2012
years.h: Cradle Spell of Fall River closes the collected works
years.p: A single track, and the last entry in Ott's Grace Period archive.

eras.title: Back catalog, Cape Cod and college radio
eras.text: Audio Dregs put Dynasty online, the Four Tet remix made it onto a box set, and Old Colony came back as Mutual Skies. The Grace Period itself only surfaces now and then.

years.src: Audio Dregs: Dynasty (Bandcamp) · Discogs: Dynasty · AllMusic: Dynasty
years.h: Audio Dregs puts Dynasty on Bandcamp
years.p: Bandcamp shows this upload date as the release date. The CD itself is (P) 2001 and was in shops January 15, 2002.

years.src: Discogs: Elements I-V
years.h: The Four Tet remix lands in a five-CD box
years.p: There Is Love In You 82 (Angel Echoes) appears on Elements Five, part of Home Normal's Elements I-V.

years.src: Mutual Skies: The Capital Suite, Bekampa Tramset · Discogs: Old Colony Recordings · Mutual Skies: 1 Mile North, The Sunken Nest
years.h: Mutual Skies reissues the other Bekampa Tramset
years.p: The Cape Cod label, which Discogs says Old Colony now trades as, brings back the Capital Suite's 1998 album on CD and streaming. In December it releases 1 Mile North's The Sunken Nest.

years.src: SoundCloud: The Grace Period
years.h: 10 JCDE (edit) appears on SoundCloud
years.p: The newest Grace Period upload so far, more than a decade after the archive's last entry.

years.src: WPRB: Hidden Lands, Aug 15, 2024
years.h: WPRB plays I Can See My Breath
years.p: Princeton's college station spins the Dynasty track on DJ Hog's Hidden Lands show, 22 years after the CD.
